tagline: Single-lane gravel crosses sagebrush hills between Ravendale and Duck Flat.
intro: Buckhorn is a BLM Back Country Byway across a high plateau of rolling sagebrush hills and intermittent lakes. The road is single-lane gravel, with views north to the South Warner Mountains. FHWA allows two hours for the drive and highlights wild horse habitat, seasonal waterfowl and ponderosa pines growing in dunes off the byway.

At its California end, Ravendale was a station on the Nevada-California-Oregon Railway. The country crossed by the road is also managed for wild horses and burros: in 2022, BLM announced a Twin Peaks gather to reduce herds that it said exceeded its established population range.

From Ravendale on US 395, the drive crosses the plateau toward Highway 447 at the edge of Duck Flat. Sagebrush hills and intermittent lakes form the route’s high-country passage between those two highways.

moments.title: Ravendale
moments.text: Ravendale anchors the byway at US 395 between Susanville and Alturas. The settlement was a station on the Nevada-California-Oregon Railway, and its post office opened in 1910. The post office closed in 1920 and reopened the next year.

moments.title: The sagebrush plateau
moments.text: The gravel road crosses rolling hills covered in sagebrush, with intermittent lakes and the South Warner Mountains visible to the north. FHWA identifies the wet-weather lakes just off the byway as stops for migrating birds during wet months. The route also crosses the Twin Peaks Wild Horse and Burro Management Area.

moments.title: Duck Flat
moments.text: The Nevada end meets Highway 447 at the edge of Duck Flat. BLM’s brochure describes the opposite-direction approach from here as a climb onto the high plateau. The change from the flat to the rolling sagebrush hills is part of the road’s documented character.

practical: Ravendale: FHWA advises a four-wheel-drive vehicle, extra water and a spare tire for this drive. (checked 2026-10-20)
